arxiv-2012-05329.title: Know Your Limits: Uncertainty Estimation with ReLU Classifiers Fails at Reliable OOD Detection
arxiv-2012-05329.creator: Dennis Ulmer, Giovanni Cinà
arxiv-2012-05329.description: Abstract A crucial requirement for reliable deployment of deep learning models for safety-critical applications is the ability to identify out-of-distribution (OOD) data points, samples which differ from the training data and on which a model might underperform. Previous work has attempted to tackle this problem using uncertainty estimation techniques.

arxiv-2209-04867.title: Large covariance matrix estimation by penalized log-det heuristics Thanks: We thank the participants to the Conference ”Mathematical Methods of Modern Statistics 3”, held in Luminy (France) in June 2022, where a preliminary version of this work was presented, for their encouragement and constructive
arxiv-2209-04867.creator: Enrico Bernardi
arxiv-2209-04867.description: Abstract This paper provides a comprehensive estimation framework for large covariance matrices via a log-det heuristics augmented by a nuclear norm plus ℓ 1 \ell_{1} -norm penalty. We develop the model framework, which includes high-dimensional approximate factor models with a sparse residual covariance.

arxiv-2210-01992.title: Capturing the dynamics of a two orifice silo with the μ ⁡ ( I ) \mu(I) model and extensions Journal: Advanced Powder Technology
arxiv-2210-01992.creator: Samuel K Irvine, Luke A Fullard, Daniel J Holland, Daniel A Clarke, Thomasin A Lynch, Pierre-Yves Lagrée
arxiv-2210-01992.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Samuel K Irvine, Luke A Fullard, Daniel J Holland, Daniel A Clarke, Thomasin A Lynch, Pierre-Yves Lagrée. Granular material in a silo with two openings can display a ‘flow rate dip’, where a non-monotonic relationship between flow rate and orifice separation occurs. In this paper we study continuum modelling of the silo with two openings. We find that the μ ⁡ ( I ) \mu(I) rheology can capture the flow rate dip if physically relevant friction parameters are used.

arxiv-2211-04330.title: Non-adiabatic Ring Polymer Molecular Dynamics in the Phase Space of the S ​ U ​ ( N ) {SU}(N) Lie Group
arxiv-2211-04330.creator: Duncan Bossion, Sutirtha N. Chowdhury, Pengfei Huo
arxiv-2211-04330.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Duncan Bossion, Sutirtha N. Chowdhury, Pengfei Huo. We derive the non-adiabatic ring polymer molecular dynamics (RPMD) approach in the phase space of the S ​ U ​ ( N ) {SU}(N) Lie Group. This method, which we refer to as the spin mapping non-adiabatic RPMD (SM-NRPMD), is based on the spin-mapping formalism for the electronic degrees of freedom (DOFs) and ring polymer path-integral description for the nuclear DOFs.

arxiv-2305-16018.title: Accommodating informative visit times for analysing irregular longitudinal data: a sensitivity analysis approach with balancing weights estimators
arxiv-2305-16018.creator: Sean Yiu and Li Su
arxiv-2305-16018.description: Abstract Irregular longitudinal data with informative visit times arise when patients’ visits are partly driven by concurrent disease outcomes. However, existing methods such as inverse intensity weighting (IIW), often overlook or have not adequately assess the influence of informative visit times on estimation and inference.

arxiv-2311-07073.title: Exposition on over-squashing problem on GNNs: Current Methods, Benchmarks and Challenges
arxiv-2311-07073.creator: Dai Shi, Andi Han, Lequan Lin, Yi Guo, Junbin Gao
arxiv-2311-07073.description: Abstract Graph-based message-passing neural networks (MPNNs) have achieved remarkable success in both node and graph-level tasks. However, several identified problems including over-smoothing (OSM), limited expressive power, and over-squashing (OSQ), still restrain the performance of MPNNs. In particular, the latest identified problem, OSQ, reveals that MPNNs generally cannot promise their learning accuracy with tasks that require long-range dependencies between node pairs.

arxiv-2409-11416.title: The Unseen AI Disruptions for Power Grids: LLM-Induced Transients
arxiv-2409-11416.creator: Yuzhuo Li, Mariam Mughees, Yize Chen, Yunwei Ryan Li
arxiv-2409-11416.description: Abstract Recent breakthroughs of large language models (LLMs) have exhibited superior capability across major industries and stimulated multi-hundred-billion-dollar investment in AI-centric data centers in the next 3-5 years. This, in turn, bring the increasing concerns on sustainability and AI-related energy usage.

arxiv-2505-09580.title: Phase Diagram Magnetic Features of Holographic Anisotropic Model for z 4 z^{4} -term Heavy Quarks
arxiv-2505-09580.creator: Kristina Rannu
arxiv-2505-09580.description: Abstract Thermodynamical features depending on magnetic field of the previously found five-dimensional anisotropic holographic solution for heavy quarks supported by Einstein-dilaton-three-Maxwell action with extended warp factor and improved coupling function for the Maxwell field providing chemical potential are studied. Direct/inverse magnetic catalysis behavior is considered.

arxiv-2506-23077.title: Dynamic Contrastive Learning for Hierarchical Retrieval: A Case Study of Distance-Aware Cross-View Geo-Localization PubID: pubid: 0000–0000/00$00.00 © 2021 IEEE
arxiv-2506-23077.creator: Suofei Zhang, Xinxin Wang, Xiaofu Wu, Quan Zhou, Haifeng Hu
arxiv-2506-23077.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Suofei Zhang, Xinxin Wang, Xiaofu Wu, Quan Zhou, Haifeng Hu. Existing deep learning-based cross-view geo-localization methods primarily focus on improving the accuracy of cross-domain image matching, rather than enabling models to comprehensively capture contextual information around the target and minimize the cost of localization errors. To support systematic research into this Distance-Aware Cross-View Geo-Localization (DACVGL) problem, we construct Distance-Aware Campus (DA-Campus), the first benchmark that pairs multi-view imagery with precise distance annotations across three spatial resolutions.

arxiv-2509-18843.title: Notebook for the BioASQ Lab at CLEF 2025
arxiv-2509-18843.creator: Damian Stachura, Joanna Konieczna, Artur Nowak
arxiv-2509-18843.description: Abstract Open-weight versions of large language models (LLMs) are rapidly advancing, with state-of-the-art models like DeepSeek-V3 now performing comparably to proprietary LLMs. This progression raises the question of whether small open-weight LLMs are capable of effectively replacing larger closed-source models.

arxiv-2512-05984.title: Dual-moon forced dynamics and nonlinear aggregation in Saturn’s F ring: From quasi-periodicity to modulated oscillations
arxiv-2512-05984.creator: Omar El Deeb
arxiv-2512-05984.description: Abstract We develop a minimal nonlinear model to investigate the oscillatory dynamics of Saturn’s F ring under dual-moon forcing from Prometheus and Pandora. The model extends classical predator–prey dynamics by incorporating both a nonlinear mass aggregation term k ​ M n kM^{n} and explicit dual-frequency forcing, capturing how higher-order coagulation physics interacts with multi-moon perturbations.

arxiv-2603-07367.creator: Douglas MacMyn Brown, Alexander Mietke

plos-pone-0008235.creator: Edward O. Ronan, Lian Ni Lee, Peter C. L. Beverley et al.
plos-pone-0008235.description: PLOS ONE research article. In pulmonary Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) infection, immune responses are delayed compared to other respiratory infections, so that antigen-specific cells are not detected in the lungs earlier than day 14. Even after parenteral immunization with Bacille Calmette Guerin (BCG)

pmc-10591418.title: Comparative analyses of dynamic transcriptome profiles highlight key response genes and dominant isoforms for muscle development and growth in chicken
pmc-10591418.creator: Zhang Wang, Weihua Tian, Dandan Wang, Yulong Guo, Zhimin Cheng, Yanyan Zhang, Xinyan Li, Yihao Zhi, Donghua Li, Zhuanjian Li, Ruirui Jiang, Guoxi Li, Yadong Tian, Xiangtao Kang, Hong Li, Ian C. Dunn, Xiaojun Liu
pmc-10591418.description: BackgroundModern breeding strategies have resulted in significant differences in muscle mass between indigenous chicken and specialized broiler. However, the molecular regulatory mechanisms that underlie these differences remain elusive. The aim of this study was to identify key genes and regulatory mechanisms underlying differences in breast muscle development between indigenous chicken and specialized broiler.

pmc-10642011.title: Exploring the association between circRNA expression and pediatric obesity based on a case–control study and related bioinformatics analysis
pmc-10642011.creator: Guobo Li, Xingyan Xu, Le Yang, Yingying Cai, Yi Sun, Jianhui Guo, Yawen Lin, Yuduan Hu, Mingjun Chen, Huangyuan Li, Siying Wu
pmc-10642011.description: ObjectiveOur present study utilized case–control research to explore the relationship between specific circRNAs and pediatric obesity through a literature review and bioinformatics and to predict their possible biological functions, providing ideas for epigenetic mechanism studies of pediatric obesity.MethodsCircRNAs related to pediatric obesity were preliminarily screened by a literature review and qRT–PCR.

pmc-11390887.title: Effects of MAFLD defined by fatty liver index or ultrasonography on kidney function decline in the general population
pmc-11390887.creator: Yu-Ji Lee, Kwang Min Kim, Nak Gyeong Ko, Mihyeon Jin, Jin Hee Na, In Ho Park
pmc-11390887.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). This study aimed to investigate whether metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) defined by the fatty liver index (FLI) affects the decline in kidney function and whether this relationship is still observed in MAFLD defined by ultrasonography (USG). A retrospective cohort study was conducted using de-identified data from participants who received health checkups at Samsung Changwon Hospital between 2002 and 2018. The primary and secondary exposures were the presence of FLI- and USG-defined MAFLD, respectively.

pmc-11413018.title: Demonstration of shape analysis of neutron resonance transmission spectrum measured with a laser-driven neutron source
pmc-11413018.creator: Mitsuo Koizumi, Fumiaki Ito, Jaehong Lee, Kota Hironaka, Tohn Takahashi, Satoshi Suzuki, Yasunobu Arikawa, Yuki Abe, Zechen Lan, Tianyun Wei, Takato Mori, Takehito Hayakawa, Akifumi Yogo
pmc-11413018.description: Laser-driven neutron sources (LDNSs) can generate strong short-pulse neutron beams, which are valuable for scientific studies and engineering applications. Neutron resonance transmission analysis (NRTA) is a nondestructive technique used for determining the areal density of each nuclide in a material sample using pulsed thermal and epithermal neutrons.

pmc-11486809.title: H+-translocating pyrophosphatases in protozoan parasites
pmc-11486809.creator: Karina Araujo-Ruiz, Ricardo Mondragón-Flores
pmc-11486809.description: Integral membrane pyrophosphatases (mPPases) hydrolyze pyrophosphate. This enzymatic mechanism is coupled with the pumping of H + and/or Na + across membranes, which can be either K + -dependent or K + -independent. Inorganic proton–translocating pyrophosphatases (H + -PPases) can transport protons across cell membranes and are reported in various organisms such as plants, bacteria, and protozoan parasites.

pmc-11489765.title: Molecular mechanisms of re-emerging chloramphenicol susceptibility in extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Enterobacterales
pmc-11489765.creator: Fabrice E. Graf, Richard N. Goodman, Sarah Gallichan, Sally Forrest, Esther Picton-Barlow, Alice J. Fraser, Minh-Duy Phan, Madalitso Mphasa, Alasdair T. M. Hubbard, Patrick Musicha, Mark A. Schembri, Adam P. Roberts, Thomas Edwards, Joseph M. Lewis, Nicholas A. Feasey
pmc-11489765.description: Infections with Enterobacterales (E) are increasingly difficult to treat due to antimicrobial resistance. After ceftriaxone replaced chloramphenicol (CHL) as empiric therapy for suspected sepsis in Malawi in 2004, extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-E rapidly emerged. Concurrently, resistance to CHL in Escherichia coli and Klebsiella spp. decreased, raising the possibility of CHL re-introduction.

pmc-11641929.title: Italian XEN-Glaucoma Treatment Registry (XEN-GTR): Effectiveness and Safety at 36 Months of XEN45 Implant
pmc-11641929.creator: Francesco Oddone, Gloria Roberti, Sara Giammaria, Chiara Posarelli, Leonardo Mastropasqua, Luca Agnifili, Tommaso Micelli Ferrari, Vincenzo Pace, Matteo Sacchi, Romeo Altafini, Gianluca Scuderi, Andrea Perdicchi, Carmela Carnevale, Antonio Fea, Michele Figus, Eun Ji Lee
pmc-11641929.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Objectives: We evaluated the 3-year effectiveness and safety of XEN45, combined or not with phacoemulsification, in patients from the Italian XEN-Glaucoma Treatment Registry. Methods: Data from glaucoma patients who underwent XEN45 alone or combined with phacoemulsification were analyzed. Changes in intraocular pressure (IOP) and the number of ocular hypotensive medications (OHMs) were tested with repeated measures ANOVA in last observation carried forward (LOCF) and per-protocol (PP) analyses.

pmc-12538996.title: Effect of a virtual reality simulator for preclinical instruction of operative dentistry on level of competence of undergraduate dental students
pmc-12538996.creator: Mohammad Mehdi Heidaridarani, Fatemeh Farzaneh, Gita Rezvani, Soleiman Ahmady, Fahimeh Dehestani Ardakani, Mohammad Hossein Mahrooz
pmc-12538996.description: BackgroundThis study aimed to assess the effect of a virtual reality (VR) simulator for instruction of restorative dentistry on the level of competence of undergraduate dental students.MethodsThis case-control study was conducted on 55 third-year dental students, who were randomly assigned to the intervention (n = 30) and control (n = 25) groups.

pmc-12550055.title: Research on the design of overall stability capacity for axial compression and single sided connected eccentric compression equal leg angles
pmc-12550055.creator: JingJing Han, Wei Zhang, LuFeng Yang
pmc-12550055.description: This study investigates the design methods for the overall stability capacity in equal-leg angles under axial compression and those subjected to eccentric compression with single-sided connections. It compares eight current codes from China, Europe, Australia, and the United States, emphasizing the differing design considerations for equal-leg angles.

pmc-12647146.title: Robust and imperceptible image watermarking using chaotic map-integrated quantum-inspired multi-objective cuckoo search optimization
pmc-12647146.creator: Prati Dubey, Abdul Khader Jilani Saudagar, Ramesh Chandra Poonia, Mukesh Asati
pmc-12647146.description: With the rapid growth of multimedia data transmission for secure and reliable communication has become critical due to increasing cyber threats. This paper presents a Chaotic Map-integrated Quantum-Inspired Multi-Objective Cuckoo Search (CMQICS)-based watermarking approach to achieve high imperceptibility, robustness, and embedding efficacy. The proposed approach integrates quantum-inspired cuckoo search optimization with chaotic mapping to enhance watermark embedding.

pmc-12791843.title: Early Intervention vs Conservative Management in Severe Asymptomatic Aortic Stenosis
pmc-12791843.creator: Victor Dayan, Mateo Marin-Cuartas, Raffaele De Caterina, Suzanne De Waha, Nicolas M Van Mieghem, Michael A Borger, Robert O Bonow, Deepak L Bhatt
pmc-12791843.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Aortic stenosis (AS) is a progressive disease that may remain asymptomatic despite underlying myocardial damage. Management of asymptomatic severe AS remains controversial, especially in the current era of safer surgical and transcatheter valve replacement.

pmc-13123463.title: Distinctive domestication of farmhouse beer yeasts preserved pre-industrial genetic and phenotypic diversity
pmc-13123463.creator: Peter W. Bircham, Andrea Del Cortona, Lars Marius Garshol, Mohammed T. Tawfeeq, Beatriz Herrera-Malaver, Sofie Mannaerts, Jeroen Cortebeeck, Robbe Nolmans, Brigida Gallone, Anton Gorkovskiy, Michael Abrouk, Jan Steensels, Kevin J. Verstrepen
pmc-13123463.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummarySince its inception over 10,000 years ago, beer brewing has transformed from a domestic activity based on uncontrolled spontaneous fermentations into a highly optimized industrial process that uses pure single-strain starter cultures of Saccharomyces yeasts. Along with the storage of frozen yeast stocks, this shift halted the domestication process of beer yeasts and led to a massive loss of beer yeast biodiversity.

pmc-13313365.title: Cultural capital and health literacy among urban communities in Malaysia: A cross-sectional study
pmc-13313365.creator: Nurul Izyan Husna Ibrahim, Abdul Hafiz Ab Rahman, Azlina Abdullah, Shamarina Shohaimi, Kristiawan Indriyanto, Kristiawan Indriyanto, Kristiawan Indriyanto, Kristiawan Indriyanto, Kristiawan Indriyanto
pmc-13313365.description: Health literacy is an important determinant of health outcomes, yet many approaches continue to emphasize individual cognitive skills while giving limited attention to the sociocultural resources that shape how people engage with health information. This study examined the association between cultural capital and multiple dimensions of health literacy among urban communities in Malaysia.

pmc-13405095.title: Impact of semaglutide withdrawal on cardiometabolic profile and physiology of energy balance: Recovery effects after semaglutide termination – The REST trial study protocol
pmc-13405095.creator: Taras Yevusiak, Alanna Weisman, Ravi Retnakaran, Sean Wharton, Daniel J. Drucker, Caroline K. Kramer

pmc-13411946.creator: Anupam Debnath, Bidhan C Das, Murshidul Arefin, Md Kawsar Bhuiyan, Golam Mahmud Rayhan, Nur Alam Mohim, Amit Chowdhury, Azfar Bin Anis, Ondrila Debnath Oishi, Mohsen Chowdhury

pmc-13518249.title: Targeting HDAC and proteostasis to eradicate quiescent cancer cells
pmc-13518249.creator: Qi Jiang, Michelle Ertel, Austin Arrigo, Amjad Hijazzi, Sara Sannino, Jennifer L. Goeckeler-Fried, April Sagan, Ian Beddows, Betsy Ann Varghese, Daniel D. Brown, Wayne Stallaert, Adrian Lee, Amanda M. Clark, Hui Shen, Jeffrey L. Brodsky, Hatice U. Osmanbeyoglu, Ronald J. Buckanovich
pmc-13518249.description: Chemotherapy remains the primary treatment for ovarian cancer (OvCa), and chemoresistance drives patient mortality. Cellular quiescence, reversible exit from the cell cycle, increases chemotherapy resistance as chemotherapies primarily target rapidly proliferating cells. Here, we report that CHD4 and MBD3, components of the nucleosome remodeling and deacetylase (NuRD) complex, are downregulated in quiescent OvCa cells (qOvCa).

pmc-13554924.title: Heterozygous TSHR Variants in Pediatric Idiopathic Subclinical Hypothyroidism: Association with a Variable and Compensated Thyroid Phenotype
pmc-13554924.creator: Ayşe Yaşar, Murat Hakkı Yarar, Heves Kırmızıbekmez, Fatma Dursun
pmc-13554924.description: ObjectiveSubclinical hypothyroidism (SH) in childhood is frequently idiopathic and usually follows a benign course. Heterozygous loss-of-function variants in the thyrotropin receptor (TSHR) gene have emerged as a genetic cause of isolated hyperthyrotropinemia but data regarding long-term outcomes and management are limited.MethodsWe retrospectively evaluated children (aged 1-18 years) diagnosed with idiopathic SH.
